thread:
sara_support: Heads-up — customer Velox Labs (prod, eu-west) opened a ticket: sustained 429s, looks like they hit a per-minute cap. They say traffic is steady ~25 rps but they only get a few successful responses at the top of each minute and then a flood of 429s for ~20-30s. Request ids: rx-9f3a2, rx-9f3a3.

eli_eng: Thanks — can you grab one raw request+response (with headers) and a short timeline? We need the x-rate-limit headers (or whichever we return) and whether this is HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.

sara_support: Pasted from customer (redacted):
```
HTTP/2 429 \ndate: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 03:11:00 GMT
content-type: application/json
request-id: rx-9f3a2
x-rate-limit-rpm: 1200
x-rate-limit-tpm: 72000
x-rate-limit-remaining-rpm: 0
body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"minute capacity exhausted"}
```
They did confirm they're using http2 multiplexing from a single host.

mohit_sre: Interesting — remaining-rpm:0 indicates the minute bucket drained. Need to check if requests are bunched at the top of each minute on their side. Ask them if they have any cron/minutely batches, worker restarts, or SDKs that refill counters at boundary.

kai_support: Also ask whether they use connection pooling vs new connections per request. If they open many concurrent streams over one connection the server-side accounting can cause effective bursts that align to minute boundaries.

eli_eng: Quick repro command we can ask them to run to prove minute-boundary folding: run a short concurrent curl loop that sleeps to align to top-of-minute, e.g.
```
# align to next minute then blast 100 concurrent requests
sleep $((60 - $(date +%s) % 60))
for i in {1..100}; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done; wait
```
If many 429s show immediately after the minute start we've reproduced the symptom.

sara_support: Customer ran something similar and attached a small flamegraph of requests — they show a spike at 03:10:00 UTC. They also said their client SDK has an exponential backoff but with very short initial backoff so many clients retry quickly, making the burst worse.

mohit_sre: Two-pronged plan: 1) short-term mitigation steps for customer, 2) infra checks on our side. For the customer: reduce retry concurrency, add randomized jitter on retry, increase initial backoff to 500ms, and enable token-bucket smoothing if available. Ask them to try windowed client-side pacing (spread requests across minute).

eli_eng: On infra: I'll check the per-tenant token bucket implementation and logs for the tenant id around the timestamps (03:09:58–03:11:10). Looking for: sudden refill events, dropped keepalives, or proxy-layer mis-attribution that funnels many workers into one logical key.

kai_support: Customer also asked whether Dedicated/Dedicated+ through Redwood fixes this — remind them that Dedicated gives higher reserved throughput and predictable capacity, but doesn't eliminate minute-boundary client-side bursts if the client floods faster than the reservation.

sara_support: Customer provided a replay token and sample trace: https://replay.redwood/velox/rx-9f3a2 — gave us permission to replay in staging.

mohit_sre: I'll replay in staging with a few client patterns: single-host heavy multiplex, multi-host low-concurrency, and naive retry-loop. Will share a short log snippet.

deploy-bot: replay job started (id: replay-5521). Logs available in /staging/replays/replay-5521.

eli_eng: If replay reproduces, check whether our edge proxy is folding minute buckets per connection or per-tenant key. If per-connection, http2 multiplexing could accidentally concentrate accounting. If per-tenant, then we need to inspect ratecap service metrics (burst counters, refill jitter).

mohit_sre: Also to check: are we returning Retry-After or header-based quotas? Customer saw only the 429 body. If we return a Retry-After or an x-retry-after-ms header that helps clients implement respectful backoff.

sara_support: Customer asked for a recommended SDK backoff snippet — suggested: initial 500ms, jitter 0-300ms, max 10s, and exponential factor 2, with circuit breaker after 5 successive 429s to pause for next full-minute slot. They liked that.

eli_eng: Action items:
- sara_support: collect a redacted HAR or raw headers for request ids rx-9f3a2/3 and any other samples.
- mohit_sre: run replay-5521 and paste brief results + tenant token-bucket logs.
- kai_support: send recommended backoff/config snippet to Velox + doc links on "Avoid minute-boundary folding".

sara_support: Will ask customer to try updated backoff and run the curl blast test. I'll update thread when they confirm. :thumbsup:

mohit_sre: Replay finished — staging shows identical behavior when client blasts 120rps aligned to minute boundary: token bucket drained in ~6s, remainder returned 429s until next refill. Logs: "tenant=velox buckets: rpm_remaining=0 at 03:10:06, refill at 03:11:00". Sharing sanitized log snippet:
```
[03:10:05] tenant=velox tokens=15/1200
[03:10:06] tenant=velox tokens=0 -> 429 responses start
[03:10:45] tenant=velox tokens=0
[03:11:00] tenant=velox refill +1200 tokens
```

eli_eng: Conclusion: behavior matches expected rate-limiter semantics. Recommend customer-side smoothing + SDK backoff. For a platform change we can consider adding per-tenant jittered refill or micro-refills to reduce the cliff (but that affects strict rpm accounting). I'll open a follow-up RFC if product wants to soften minute cliff.

sara_support: Customer will try client changes; if problems persist we'll discuss quota bump or Dedicated reservation. Closing interim, will reopen if they still see 429s after changes.
